name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: Iran threat to Gulf cables; GNSS jamming
summary: Iranian officials suggest Gulf undersea cables could be targeted; GNSS jamming persists
state: Iranian officials suggested on 4 Nov that undersea cables in the Gulf and European countries could be targeted (Al Jazeera). GNSS jamming remains widespread in the Gulf and Baltic. No new cable cut had been reported as of 4 Nov; the Philippines–Singapore link repair continues.
for_you: No action needed for most users. Firms reliant on Gulf data routes may face disruption if cables are hit.
rubric_hit: Widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation = Watch; no new cuts

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran says US reply unconvincing; threats to Gulf cables

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
